title: Tech Note: User Changeable Output Form

historical_commentary.text: This is the first note in the output-form-customization series (later extended by "User Preferences"), demonstrating how to let end users pick which fields populate each output form column, along with per-column header text, number/date/time/boolean formatting, and alignment, all driven at runtime by four layout variables per column and one reusable method. This kind of dynamic, end-user-configurable list view remains a legitimate and common feature request today, but modern 4D development would typically implement it using List Box object/collection column configuration rather than classic output form layout variables.
related_updates: Modern dynamic/user-configurable tabular views in 4D are generally built with the List Box object's programmatic column and data-source APIs (introduced/expanded well after 2005) rather than classic output form layout variables

The follow-up 'User Preferences' Tech Note (05-28) extended this exact technique to persist choices to a table — that persistence approach has itself since been superseded by JSON/object-based settings storage
